acceptance: Dependency admission occurs before identity implementation: Cargo manifests/lock and third_party/dependencies/approved.json pin ed25519-dalek 3.0.0, getrandom 0.4.3, and zeroize 1.9.0 exactly; default features are disabled, required license exceptions are documented, cargo metadata/license observations match approvals, dependency validation passes, and no identity code lands before the admitted dependency slice is post-merge qualified.

InstallationId is exactly 16 bytes, production generation uses getrandom OS entropy, canonical external text is exactly 32 lowercase hex characters, invalid/alternate encodings reject without normalization, and InstallationId is non-secret and never treated as authority.

Active identity key creation obtains a fresh 32-byte seed from getrandom and constructs a valid Ed25519 SigningKey. The public descriptor exposes exactly the corresponding 32-byte verifying key plus InstallationId and positive generation, while private material has no Debug/Display/serde/log/evidence/filesystem exposure.

Key generation starts at 1, rotation increments exactly once with checked arithmetic, zero and overflow reject fail-closed, InstallationId remains stable across rotation, and the new verifying key differs from the retired public key under executable tests.

Rotation creates fresh OS-random secret material, produces explicit previous/current public lineage, signs/verifies with the new key, does not silently retain or reactivate the retired private key, and does not imply remote revocation or Grant authority.

RecoverySeed is exactly 32 secret bytes, zeroizes on drop, exposes no secret-revealing formatting/serialization, and recovery reconstructs the expected key only when the derived verifying key equals the supplied expected descriptor. Wrong seed/public-key/generation/install-id combinations fail with typed non-secret errors.

IdentitySessionBinding uses an exact domain/version separator and cryptographically binds InstallationId, positive key generation, exact 16-byte InstanceId, exact 32-byte SessionChallenge, verifying key, and Ed25519 signature. Verification succeeds for an exact binding and fails if any bound field, domain/version, key, challenge, or signature changes.

InstanceId production generation uses OS randomness and exact strict 32-lowercase-hex external form. SessionChallenge is caller-supplied exact 32 bytes and is not itself an authorization token or persistent secret store.

The public API provides no generic arbitrary-message signing function, no private-key byte export, no Grant/policy signing, and no durable secret-storage API. Repository source assertions and manual security review verify those negative surfaces.

Ubuntu workspace tests, local macOS tests, and the existing native Windows kernuxd CI job execute kernux-identity creation/rotation/recovery/session-binding tests successfully. Cross-compilation alone is not accepted as Windows runtime evidence.
KRP schema/generated Rust/TypeScript outputs, T02 launch-nonce authentication, and kernuxd local transport behavior remain unchanged and existing protocol/auth/runtime regression suites remain PASS.

The exact bounded candidates pass git diff --check, full pnpm check, dependency/provenance validation where applicable, Diffcipline R3, Alibaba OpenCodeReview Delegation Mode plus complete manual accounting for exclusions, all five protected exact-head checks, and the additive Windows kernuxd job.

After native SpecGrain verification and protected closeout merge/post-merge qualification, KX-P02-S02-T01 becomes PROVEN; only KX-P02-S03-T01 may become NEXT if canonical live truth still confirms that dependency-ordered frontier, all later P02 tasks remain PLANNED, and P02 phase exit remains unproven.

minimality.rationale: The canonical architecture names a dedicated kernux-identity crate, but no repository identity implementation exists. Reuse the proven T02 security/governance boundaries and existing CI; admit only Ed25519, OS-randomness, and zeroization dependencies needed for real local key lifecycle primitives. Do not add storage, credential-provider, policy, remote-trust, or generic crypto framework layers.

requirements: Private Ed25519 seed/signing material and RecoverySeed must never be serialized, logged, formatted, written to repository evidence, passed through argv/environment, or persisted by this task; secret wrappers must zeroize on drop.

Production identity creation, key rotation, and InstanceId generation must use operating-system randomness; deterministic seeds are allowed only in explicit tests/recovery inputs and must never silently replace production RNG.
Recovery must fail closed unless the supplied secret reconstructs the exact expected verifying key and bound identity generation; errors must not expose secret bytes or matching-prefix information.
Session binding must be domain-separated and field-complete so tampering or cross-protocol reuse cannot silently verify.
Local identity/key possession in this task does not itself grant policy authority, privileged host operations, remote trust, secret access, or P02 phase completion.

outcome: Create a provider-neutral Kernux local identity crate that establishes stable installation identity, real Ed25519 key creation, checked key rotation and recovery, and domain-separated instance/session binding primitives using OS randomness, while explicitly deferring durable persistence, OS credential-store integration, policy/grants, remote enrollment, and later P02 authority.
rationale: KX-P02-S01-T02 is PROVEN and post-merge-qualified, and KX-P02-S02-T01 is the only authorized frontier. The canonical architecture names a dedicated kernux-identity crate and the master plan requires installation/device identity plus key lifecycle primitives before metadata storage, policy, secrets, or remote enrollment.

risk.recovery: Revert only the bounded SG-000020 refinement/implementation/closeout changes, remove kernux-identity and any newly admitted direct dependency entries/lock changes, restore the prior Windows CI commands, keep KX-P02-S02-T01 at NEXT, and preserve SG-000019/T02 proof. No later P02 authority is created by rollback.

scope_in: Create the repository-owned crates/kernux-identity Rust library as the sole bounded implementation surface for local installation/device identity primitives in this task; do not couple the new crate to kernuxd transport or later policy/store crates.

Before identity implementation, separately admit exact runtime dependencies ed25519-dalek = 3.0.0, getrandom = 0.4.3, and zeroize = 1.9.0 through the repository dependency registry and a task-specific license/dependency evidence packet. Use exact pins and default-features = false; enable only ed25519-dalek zeroize support unless a reviewed implementation need proves another feature necessary.

Define InstallationId as an opaque non-secret exact 16-byte value with strict 32-lowercase-hex canonical text. Production creation obtains all 16 bytes from the operating-system RNG through getrandom; parsing rejects wrong length, uppercase, non-hex, whitespace, and alternate encodings. Knowledge of the ID grants no authority.

Define an explicit positive key generation counter starting at 1 with checked increment and no zero/wraparound semantics. Key generation is identity lineage metadata, not time, authorization, or ordering authority.

Represent the active device key as an Ed25519 SigningKey created from a fresh 32-byte OS-random seed. Expose only a non-secret public descriptor containing installation identity, generation, and the exact 32-byte Ed25519 verifying key in strict 64-lowercase-hex form. Do not expose secret bytes through Debug, Display, serde, logs, errors, evidence, or ordinary public accessors.

Implement checked key rotation that preserves InstallationId, increments generation exactly once, creates a fresh independent Ed25519 key using OS randomness, returns bounded previous/current public descriptors for lineage, and does not retain the previous secret key after the rotation result is established.

Implement recovery from an explicitly supplied RecoverySeed secret wrapper plus expected InstallationId, generation, and verifying-key descriptor. The recovery seed is exactly 32 bytes, zeroizes on drop, has no secret-revealing formatting/serialization, reconstructs the same Ed25519 key only when the expected public key matches, and otherwise fails with a generic non-secret typed error.

Implement a domain-separated IdentitySessionBinding primitive that signs exactly the current InstallationId, key generation, fresh InstanceId, and caller-supplied 32-byte SessionChallenge. InstanceId is a non-secret exact 16-byte OS-random value with strict 32-lowercase-hex form. Verification must reject any tampering of installation id, generation, instance id, challenge, verifying key, domain/version, or signature.

Keep signing authority narrow: expose signing only for the identity session-binding contract in this task. Do not expose a generic arbitrary-message signing service, Grant signing, marketplace signing, remote enrollment certificate issuance, or policy authority.

Extend the existing additive Windows kernuxd CI job without renaming protected contexts so it also runs kernux-identity Clippy/tests natively on windows-latest. Ubuntu workspace CI plus local macOS qualification and the Windows job together provide cross-platform OS-RNG and Ed25519 runtime evidence.

Add deterministic/adversarial tests using synthetic recovery seeds where deterministic vectors are required, while production create/rotate paths must use the real OS RNG. Prove strict external encodings, generation overflow rejection, recovery mismatch rejection, binding tamper rejection, rotation lineage, secret non-exposure, and no accidental persistence/serialization surface.

After native verification and protected closeout, mark only KX-P02-S02-T01 PROVEN and advance only KX-P02-S03-T01 to NEXT if canonical live truth still identifies it as the next dependency-ordered frontier. P02 phase exit remains unproven.
scope_out: Do not implement SQLite, filesystem-backed identity state, durable metadata, migrations, WAL, artifact CAS, or any persistence/restart durability claim. KX-P02-S03-T01 and later storage work own durability.

Do not integrate macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager/DPAPI, Linux Secret Service/libsecret, TPM/Secure Enclave, HSM, or any other credential store. KX-P02-S06-T01 owns OS/provider secret persistence.

Do not implement capability policy, Grant issuance/enforcement, permission profiles, secret brokerage, security-audit persistence, privileged filesystem/process/PTY operations, sandbox management, browser/computer control, or any later P02 task.

Do not implement remote device enrollment, mutual TLS, remote trust establishment, cloud identity, organization/user/team identity, pairing, certificate authorities, revocation distribution, or remote transport. Later P10/P14 work owns remote and organization trust.
Do not change KRP schemas, generated Rust/TypeScript protocol bytes, T02 launch-nonce authentication, local transport semantics, or kernuxd authorization behavior in this task.
Do not add PEM, PKCS#8, serde secret serialization, plaintext key files, environment-variable secrets, command-line key material, passphrase backup formats, or export APIs for private signing keys.
Do not claim that an in-memory identity survives restart. Recovery primitives reconstruct caller-supplied material but no durable storage source is implemented here.
title: KX-P02-S02-T01 — Establish local installation identity and key lifecycle
